result.title: Which Differences Matter? Controlled Tests of Rule Transfer, Joint Reliability, and Information Use in Decision Models
result.summary: Decision models map stated rules and observed states to discrete answers. Aggregate accuracy leaves unresolved which rule and information changes guide those answers. We connect controlled input changes to transfer, joint reliability, and directed information use through executable arithmetic rules. Semantic rule separation and crossed rule and state tests make transfer and joint success separately measurable. We compare equivalent wordings, calibrate joint correctness through marginal-preserving reassociation, and alter tables to define alternative answer targets. Adaptation gains increase with nearest-source answer agreement; fully conflicting quartets yield small pooled gains and different gain signs across source splits. Equivalent rewrites have opposing task-level effects, linking transfer gains to rule presentation. Joint-score departures depend on which rule and state associations the reference preserves. A decision service changes answers more across equivalent wordings than across identical-text repeats and usually follows the answer targets implied by altered table values or mappings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以可执行算术规则为试验床，通过语义等价改写、规则与状态的交叉测试、修改表格以设定替代答案目标等受控输入变换，分离测量决策模型的规则迁移、联合正确性与定向信息使用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「受控改写＋交叉条件＋替代答案目标」的诊断设计可能可供核查，用于判断 VLM/LVR 的答案究竟由视觉证据还是规则表述与文本先验驱动，但对象为符号化决策任务，需较多迁移核查。
